tasks.title: Keep files when Moodle responses are incomplete
tasks.desc:

Reviewed the synchronous commit and rollback path. 133 networking, persistence and sync tests pass, including injected failures at each publication stage, three concurrent readers, cancellation, no Finder notification on failure, replay, and SQLite subprocess termination before/after commit. tasks.title: Make database transitions and provider reset recoverable
tasks.desc:

Priority: P0, release blocker.

Evidence: AppState.resetProvider stops automatic sync, snapshots state, then uses try? to open the fallback database before removing the domain. Done when:
- Stop and await active writers, verify a complete durable snapshot and usable fallback handle before domain removal, and retain a recoverable state on every failure.
- After successful reseeding, rebind consumers and restore watchers/automatic sync; surface an actionable error if recovery fails.
- Inject failures at fallback open, domain remove/add, seed copy and schema upgrade, including process interruption and database contention.
- Old supported schemas upgrade safely; concurrent host/extension opens agree on schema and seed completion.
- A binary opening an unsupported newer schema takes a safe, explicit path; rollback never blindly overwrites a newer store.

Run fault scenarios only against disposable copies.

notes.text: Replace partial snapshots and unsafe resets with verified durable recovery, safe schema handling and fault-injected transaction tests.

Ready for review: reset drains session writers, verifies a durable complete SQLite backup and binds its fallback before removing Finder integration. Removal preserves downloaded files; legacy originals are relocated outside provider state without changing their inode, including unindexed children, so writes through an already-open file survive. Missing files, cross-volume relocation failures, and unfamiliar legacy layouts stop removal. Failure paths retain recovery state and actionable errors; newer schemas disable writes rather than silently resuming bootstrap sync.

Schema migration and whole-database restoration are atomic. Future schemas are rejected before schema/WAL changes. A bounded process lock now coordinates schema/WAL initialization after stress exposed concurrent-opening lock conversion failures. Verified: final 95 persistence tests, 40 interface/service tests including reset stages, actual Nightly app build, and 30 complete optimized persistence runs (94 tests per run before the final lock-link regression). Tests cover interruption before/after restore commit, replay, SQLite contention, missing WAL, failed migrations, concurrent openers, preserved late file writes, and reset failure stages. Evidence: build/ds04-verified-persistence-tests.log, build/ds04-final-app-build.log, build/ds04-reset-tests.log, and build/ds04-locked-persistence-*.log.

Finder reset now drains writers and verifies a complete durable fallback before removal. It preserves original personal-file inodes and downloaded data, keeps a usable recovery handle on failures, and resumes the session only when its schema is supported.

Complete helper database retirement/replacement behavior and Release/Nightly configuration isolation.

tasks.title: Qualify the major release with a soak and go/no-go record
tasks.desc:
Approve a specific release candidate only after the stability work and the current interface reviews have passed.
Priority: final release gate.

Proposed acceptance:
- Run a 48-hour signed-build soak with at least 100 sync cycles, including offline/online transitions, sleep/wake, extension restart, repeated file materialization and app relaunch.
- Before/after manifests show zero personal-file loss or corruption; no reproducible crash, hang, stuck download or permanently disabled provider remains.
- All automated suites pass for the candidate revision; signed upgrade and FN-02 results identify the same build, dependencies and tested platforms.
- Record CPU/memory trends under a fixed workload; investigate sustained growth. Every known issue has severity, reproduction and disposition.
- Zero unresolved P0/P1 stability defects at sign-off; any proposed exception requires an explicit owner decision and is not counted as a pass.
- The release owner records go/no-go, recovery instructions and symbol/artifact locations. Repeat affected checks after any candidate change.

P0 means data safety, broken core access or build/release blocker; P1 means other reliability work required before shipping. Existing website review WB-01 remains separate. Completing this card is release qualification, not publication.
